reportHintIdea: A new feature to dream up
reportLead_bug: Tell us what isn't working. The more detail, the faster we can help!

printerHelperBambuBullets: Open Settings → General → LAN Only Mode on your printer.
Note the IP, Serial Number and 8-digit Access Code shown on screen.
TigerTag connects over MQTT on your local network.
printerHelperCrealityBullets: Find the IP in Network → Printer Information.
Use your Klipper / Moonraker access password.
printerHelperElegooBullets: Find your IP in the printer's network settings. Serial number is on the printer label or Settings menu.
printerHelperFFGBullets: IP address and serial number: tap "Basic Info", bottom right of the printer's main screen.
Found it with the scan? Then the Printer ID is all you need.
printerHelperSnapBullets: Just enter the local IP shown on the Snapmaker network screen.
printerHintBambuIP: Local IP shown in LAN Only Mode.
printerHintBambuCode: 8-digit code from the LAN Only Mode screen.
printerHintBambuSerial: Listed below the access code on the same screen.
printerHintCrealityCameraUrl: Optional — the camera is usually found on its own. Only for a custom setup: the address of its video stream.
printerHintElegooSerial: Serial number from the printer's About screen.
printerHintElegooMqtt: Access code from the printer's network settings (default: 123456).
printerHintElegooSdcpIP: That’s all a Centauri Carbon needs — no serial, no code.
elgSdcpCmdRefused: The printer didn’t take that order — try again in a moment.
printerBetaNote: This connection is brand new and hasn't met every machine out there yet. Most things should just work — if a number, a button or a slot looks off, tell us on Discord and we'll sort it fast.
printerHintFFGIP: On the printer: "Basic Info", bottom right of the main screen.
printerHintFFGPassword: On the printer: gear icon → "Network Mode".

printerHintPrusaCamera: Optional. Its own IP, once “RTSP stream on local network” is on in the Prusa app.

Camera: a Buddy3D needs its local RTSP stream switched on in the Prusa app.

scaleEmptyBullet2: Takes off the empty spool's weight, so you see the filament you really have
scaleEmptyBullet3: Large touchscreen on board: Wi-Fi, calibration wizard and updates, all on the scale
scaleEmptyBullet4: Syncs to your TigerTag account, so every screen you own shows the same numbers
scaleEmptyBullet5: Recognises brand and material from its own memory — no waiting on the internet
scaleEmptyBullet6: Works completely on its own — no computer to switch on, no app to open (battery optional)

tutoBambuX1Step5: Step 2: Enable Developer mode on the printer side. Enable "Developer Mode".

tutoBambuP1Step1: Step 1: Enable LAN Only mode on the printer side. Enter the Settings page and select WLAN.

tutoBambuP1Step5: Step 2: Enable Developer mode on the printer side. After turning on LAN Only mode, click the Scroll Down button and find Developer Mode.

tutoBambuP1Step7: If you accept all related risks or consequences, scroll down to the end and click Enable.
tutoBambuP1Step8: After enabling Developer Mode, ON will be displayed. Then use the printer IP address, Serial Number and Access Code in Tiger Studio.
tutoBambuA1Step1: Step 1: Enable LAN Only Mode on the printer side. Enter the Setting page from the printer screen by clicking Setting.
tutoBambuA1Step4: Step 2: Enable Developer Mode on the printer side. Enable "Developer Mode".
tutoBambuA1Step5: Please carefully read the Important Notice. If you accept all related risks or consequences, check "I confirm reading and understanding the Important Notice above" and then select "Enable".
tutoBambuA1Step6: Once this feature is enabled, the button will turn green.
tutoBambuA1Step7: Check the printer IP address and Serial Number from the printer settings.
tutoBambuA1Step8: Use the printer IP address, Serial Number and Access Code in Tiger Studio.
tutoFlashforgeAd5xStep1: Step 1: On the main interface, tap the "Basic Info" button at the bottom right of the screen.

linkedChipTitle: What would you like to do?
linkedChipOfferInfo: A simple link by UID to the Tags of a proprietary protocol: nothing is written into these third-party Tags.
linkedChipOfferTip: Links the detected Tags to this material.
linkedChipLinkTip: These RFID chips are already there: connect them to a material of your inventory.
linkedChipLinkBlankTip: The material is already in your inventory as a TigerData or TigerData+: it gets burned onto this blank Tag.
linkedChipLinkNeedTag: Place a blank NFC Tag on the TigerPOD: a TigerData or TigerData+ gets burned onto it and becomes a TigerTag or TigerTag+.
linkedChipLinkNeedPod: Place the material on the TigerPOD first: its blank Tag is what gets burned.
chipEraserTip: Format, recycle or write NDEF content (link, Wi‑Fi, contact…) on the chips of the TigerPOD. Nothing opens while you are here.
chipEraserToInitTip: Back to a blank TigerTag, ready for its next spool. A spool of your inventory on these chips leaves it.
chipEraserToNdefTip: A plain NFC tag (NDEF), out of the TigerTag format. A spool of your inventory on these chips leaves it.
nfcWriteNdefTip: Put a link, a Wi‑Fi network, a contact, an e‑mail, a phone number or an SMS on the chip — any phone reads it.
nfcWriteToChipTip: Writes this content onto the chips on the TigerPOD, replacing what they hold. A spool of your inventory on these chips leaves it.
nfcNdefBadUrl: That’s not a valid link — e.g. tigersystem.io or rtsp://192.168.1.20/stream.
nfcNdefTooLong: Too long for the chip: {{size}} / {{max}} bytes.
nfcNdefDone: Written. Tap a phone on it.
nfcAutoTip: Every chip you place on the TigerPOD is written right away, no hold — swap, beep, next. A spool of your inventory is never written this way.
fmtAutoTip: Every chip you place on the TigerPOD is formatted right away, no hold — swap, beep, next. A spool of your inventory is never formatted this way.
nfcAutoSkipSpool: A spool of your inventory: Auto leaves it — hold the button to write it.
chipEraserFailed: A chip didn't take it — nudge it on the reader and hold again.
linkedChipManualTip: Not in the catalogue? Brand, material and colour, typed in by hand.
linkedChipCatalogueTip: The real product, picked from the catalogue: everything is filled in for you.
linkedChipDone: Linked. Scan it and the material opens.
linkedChipUnlinkTip: Hold to unlink the chips from this material.
